title: The Moon
subject: Earth and space science

reading_level.note: docs/COPY.md: short, plain lines a 7-year-old can follow; budgets = words per line (the longest line today)

standards.note: hooks the lessons cite, not an alignment review (docs/BRAIN.md §4)

moon.idea: The Moon keeps one face to Earth. The far side gets sunlight too.

phases.idea: Why the Moon's shape changes, and what an eclipse is.

power.idea: Sunlight at the south pole, and planning for the dark.

comms.idea: Radio needs Earth in the sky. Radio words and readbacks.

radiation.idea: Solar storms, and acting on a warning in time.

life.idea: Ice in dark craters, and keeping a crew alive.

checkride.idea: Running the outpost: power, life support and radiation together.

history.idea: From Apollo to Artemis, and what each taught the next.

observe.idea: Describing a place like a geologist: size, shape, brightness.

craters.idea: Impacts and lava, and which came first.

rocks.idea: Reading the Moon's age from its rocks and surface.

fieldkit.idea: Field tools and the sampling routine.
